High Court Of Andhra Pradesh
 At Amaravati
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The Court made the following: ORDER:
This Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking the following relief:
"to issue an appropriate writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of writ of mandamus, declaring the action of the respondents in threatening to demolish the petitioners property to the extent of marking bearing D.No.3- 18/1 Ramanayyapeta, Kakinada, East Godavari District without issuing any notice as illegal and arbitrary consequently direct the respondents not to interfere with the property of the petitioner bearing D.No.3-18/1, Ramanayyapeta, Kakinada, East Godavari District and to pass such other order or orders..."
2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Government Pleader for the respondents.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the respondents are trying to demolish the property of the petitioner's without following due process of law.

4. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the 4th respondent filed a counter affidavit, wherein it is stated as follows:-
B Venkateswar Rao vs State Of Ap on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24589175/
1

entities.text: B Venkateswar Rao vs State Of Ap on 8 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "He submits that the encroachments are identified after the said survey and the same will be removed by following the due process of law since neither the 4th respondent corporation nor the other respondents undertaken any demolition work, the allegation that the respondents are threatening the demolition is not correct.

The intention of the writ petitioner behind filing of the present writ petition is to squat on the constructions, which are made encroaching the public road and to prevent the authorities from initiating action.
As on date, the respondent corporation has not initiated any steps so far and if only action, the corporation will initiate action in accordance with law".
5. On perusal of the statement made by the 4th respondent, it is only an apprehension of the petitioner, further, the respondents are not initiating any action as alleged by the petitioner as of now.

If the petitioner is identified as an encroacher they will follow due procedure as contemplated under the provisions of Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965 or the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 6. Having regard to the submissions made by the learned counsel for both the parties and on perusal of the record, this Court is of the considered view that the Writ Petition can be disposed of by directing the respondent Nos. 3 and 4, if they intend to initiate any coercive steps for the demolition of the said property purchased by the petitioner, they should follow the due procedure as contemplated under the law.
7. With the above said direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
There shall be no order as to costs.
As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions, if any, pending shall stand closed.
VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA, J 08.07.2024 klk HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA WRIT PETITION NO.16251 of 2018 08.07.2024 klk B Venkateswar Rao vs State Of Ap
